analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, docs/developer/build.md, docs/developer/test.md); no executable code, workflow or config changed, so there is no direct security regression.

prefix-cache.md: the supplied excerpt (head lines 442-862) covers only part of the change. The patch excerpt says the recurrent checkpoint bank gate now includes the plain unpublished Nemotron Super owner. It also adds `alignsRecurrentCheckpointsToPrefillChunks`, which captures only at multiples of the fixed prefill chunk.

Relevant threat: T-041, cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and the TTFT timing oracle (SEC-035). It covers the encrypted SSD tier, HMAC-keyed lookup tags, the 30-minute sliding TTL and coordinator-authored cacheSalt. The visible excerpt does not describe any change to the TTL, the lookup-tag derivation, the AAD, salt scoping or the production gate. The head text reaffirms the existing designs: DBK3 encrypted manifests bind exact token IDs and scope, and routing hints never authorize adoption without native file authentication.

The Nemotron Super checkpoint-reuse claim is documentation of code that is not in this batch. Whether the implementation adds an at-rest surface or alters demand-based admission needs a check against the real source. The new gate for Nemotron Super also depends on that unseen code.

build.md and test.md add Nemotron Super qualification sections that reference scripts/nemotron-qualification. They state that tiny-fixture passes do not qualify the shipping provider. The test.md section sits in a separate unit, with an NEMOTRON_SUPER_REFERENCE_DIR env var used only for tests. build.md lines 253-259 and test.md lines 468-486 are benign. The build.md head text appears to contain the section once, so no duplicate there.

Open item for later passes: if the PR's code changes land in other batches, check that Nemotron Super checkpoint reuse keeps the salt scoping, the identity binding and the HMAC-only on-disk names.
